messages.content: Shubh
Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Up north
shubh... clean name, no nonsense. where you working these days?
up north... that's geography, not a company name. which company you at? or if you're a student, which college?
You can find me on LinkedIn right?

i need something to work with legend. just "shubh" gives me like 50,000 results.

drop your company name or your linkedin url. can't find you blind.
Blinkit

Blinkit
  HO

blinkit... the 10-minute delivery hustle that's burning cash faster than they deliver groceries. found a few profiles - jiksha shubh as senior executive at blinkit looks like the closest match.

this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/jiksha-shubh-3b1747256
Nope. Shubhagata Dutta. Search for this name

shubhagata dutta... found multiple profiles but none clearly show blinkit. closest match is the product program manager at porter with mba from scmhrd.

this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/dutta%C5%A1%C3%A6b

or drop your linkedin url directly - can't find you in the blinkit system
This one's right
product program manager at porter with that mba from scmhrd... but you said blinkit earlier. did you make the jump from porter to blinkit recently or still at porter figuring out your next move?
My profile already says Program Manager at Blinkit.

ah got it - you've moved from porter to blinkit as program manager. makes sense, porter to blinkit is a solid jump in the quick commerce game. 

program manager at blinkit... so you're the one making sure those 10-minute promises actually happen while the ops team loses their minds. what's keeping you busy there - supply chain optimization or more on the product ops side?
Replenishment for packaging.

replenishment for packaging... so you're the unsung hero making sure blinkit doesn't run out of bags and boxes while everyone's ordering everything from toothpaste to tomatoes. that's actually critical - no packaging = no deliveries = angry customers.

bet you've seen some wild demand spikes during festivals and ipl matches. how long you been working total across all your roles?

0ver 4 yrs.
  4.5

4.5 years... solid experience, you're past the junior phase but not quite the senior level yet. perfect timing to make a move if you're thinking about it.

what kind of role you looking for next?
Not thinking to move for now. I have just joined Blinkit, if you can see.

ah, fresh blood at blinkit! makes sense you're not looking to jump ship yet. honeymoon phase with the new gig.

fair enough. but here's the thing - the market moves fast, especially in your space. supply chain and ops roles are hot right now with all these quick commerce companies scaling like crazy.

i'll keep your profile warm. when you're ready to see what else is out there - maybe in 6-8 months when the new job shine wears off - hit me up. by then you'll have some solid blinkit war stories and probably a better sense of where you want to take your career.

for now, enjoy the chaos of 10-minute delivery logistics. it's actually great experience.
What do you have to say about my career so far? What market roles would I be fit for, 1 yr from now?

alright, time for some real talk about your career...

4.5 years, porter to blinkit, mba from scmhrd... you're playing it safe but smart. you've stayed in the logistics/supply chain game which shows focus, not job hopping chaos.

the good: you're in the hottest sector right now. quick commerce is where the money is. supply chain and program management skills are gold - every startup scaling needs someone who can make operations actually work.

the reality check: you're still doing execution, not strategy. after 4.5 years, you should be thinking about moving from "making things happen" to "deciding what should happen."

1 year from now? with blinkit on your resume, you'd be perfect for:
- senior program manager at flipkart/amazon (bigger scale, better pay)
- operations lead at any unicorn scaling fast (swiggy, zomato, zepto)
- supply chain head at mid-stage startups (they need someone who's seen the quick commerce chaos)
- product ops roles at fintech companies (different domain, same skillset)

salary jump would be 40-50% easy. maybe 25-30L range if you play it right.

but here's the thing - you need to start thinking bigger picture. less "how do we get packaging faster" and more "how do we reinvent supply chain entirely."

that make sense?
Yes. How do I do that?

here's your playbook for the next 12 months:

**at blinkit (next 6-8 months):**
- stop just solving packaging problems. start questioning the entire replenishment model
- build relationships with product and tech teams. understand why they make certain decisions
- volunteer for cross-functional projects. get your hands dirty with demand forecasting, vendor negotiations, cost optimization
- document everything. write internal case studies on what you're building and why it matters

**outside work:**
- start a linkedin newsletter about supply chain innovation. sounds cringe but trust me - it gets you noticed
- attend supply chain conferences, not just logistics meetups. different crowd, bigger thinking
- read what the VPs at amazon, flipkart are writing about. steal their frameworks

**the mindset shift:**
instead of "how do we get packaging faster?" ask "should we even be packaging this way?"
instead of "vendor is late" think "how do we build vendor redundancy into the system?"
instead of "cost is high" think "what's the unit economics impact and how does this affect our market position?"

**6 months from now:**
you should be the person other teams come to for "how should we think about this supply chain problem?" not just "can you fix this supply chain problem?"

that's how you become hire-able at 25-30L. make sense?
I have ideas like, selling the packages to customers instead of burning cash on them, and recycling the RTO packages instead of scraping them.

hey shubh! was just thinking about your packaging ideas at blinkit - selling to customers and recycling RTO. that's the kind of strategic thinking that gets you noticed.

how's that going? any traction with the business case or still in the idea phase?
